description_en: Stable text identifier for joining and tracing observations. Numeric and prefixed identifiers are opaque labels and do not encode scientific meaning.
Source DOI associated with the observation; consult origin_doi and extraction_doi for provenance distinctions.
Normalized source DOI
Reported active-layer donor name; transport layers are recorded separately.
Reported active-layer acceptor name.
Normalized donor label retained from material-name matching.
Normalized acceptor label retained from material-name matching.
Donor molecular representation linked through the material reference; polymer entries generally represent finite repeat-unit surrogates.
Acceptor molecular representation linked through the material reference.
Open-circuit voltage for the observation; see metric_statistics for statistical meaning.
Short-circuit current density for the observation.
Fill factor for the observation, expressed as a percentage.

Reported PCE retained for this record, which may represent a mean, best/champion or unspecified statistic. It is not uniformly selected as the maximum PCE. Consult metric_statistics and source_notes in the linked supplement.
Derived PCE from the current complete quartet at nominal 100 mW/cm2; rounded to six decimals; not an observed irradiance or replacement for reported PCE
100 times absolute nominal calculated minus reported PCE, divided by positive reported PCE; derived diagnostic, not extraction accuracy
PCE recorded as a mean value; statistical qualifications, where present, are retained in metric_statistics and source_notes.
PCE retained in the best/champion field. Some source values lack an explicit best/champion label; consult metric_statistics and source_notes for the supported statistical meaning.
Reported donor-to-acceptor blend ratio; basis and component order are recorded separately when available.
Processing additive identity; not automatically an additional active-layer component.
Normalized processing-additive label.
Reported additive loading; interpret with its unit and basis when available.
Reported device-layer sequence or architecture description.
Reported device architecture or type label.
Electron-transport-layer material.
Retained normalized electron-transport-layer label
Hole-transport-layer material.
Retained normalized hole-transport-layer label
Reported active-layer thickness in nm. Ranges, approximations, uncertainties, explicit unit text and layer-specific values are retained as text; the field is not uniformly numeric.
Solvent used to prepare the active layer.
Retained normalized solvent label

Reported active-layer annealing temperature in degrees Celsius, not ambient preparation temperature. Any source qualifiers or nonnumeric conditions are retained as text and must not be interpreted as zero.
Donor HOMO energy annotation from the material reference unless article-specific evidence is stated.
Donor LUMO energy annotation from the material reference unless article-specific evidence is stated.
Donor band-gap annotation; interpret the optical or electrochemical basis from available source context.
Acceptor HOMO energy annotation from the material reference unless article-specific evidence is stated.
Acceptor LUMO energy annotation from the material reference unless article-specific evidence is stated.
Acceptor band-gap annotation; interpret the optical or electrochemical basis from available source context.
Stable text identifier for joining and tracing observations. Numeric and prefixed identifiers are opaque labels and do not encode scientific meaning.
Source DOI associated with the observation; consult origin_doi and extraction_doi for provenance distinctions.
Source-supported DOI of the original experimental study.
DOI of the article from which the text or table was extracted; may differ from the original experimental study.
Reported citation or reference identifying the observation source.
Source table, figure or article-text location. Web table identifiers in parentheses retain the original source anchor and need not equal a printed table number.
Source row or passage locator. Web table row numbers refer to the source web representation, not necessarily the printed table row numbering.
Source-origin classification, distinguishing original experiments and secondary quotations where established.
Active-layer composition classification, including binary controls, ternary blends or other component counts.
Material-scope label, such as organic, hybrid, inorganic or unknown.
Observation type, such as experiment, simulation, secondary quotation or unknown.
Junction or module classification, stored independently of device area.
Illumination-category label associated with the performance observation.
Reported measurement spectrum; aging conditions are not automatically measurement conditions.
Reported statistical meaning of the observation.
Per-metric statistical descriptions, stored as a JSON object or plain text. Parse valid JSON where present and otherwise retain the text; do not assume all metrics in a row share one statistic.
Reported sample count associated with a statistical result; source qualifiers may be retained.
Reported uncertainties and their statistical definitions, when available.
Reported device area; interpret the active, geometric or other area basis from source context.
Reported aperture area.
Original composition-ratio expression, preserving order and qualifiers.
Material order corresponding to a reported composition ratio, stored as a JSON array or plain text. Preserve the stated order; a partial order does not define the full blend composition.
Reported composition-ratio basis, such as mass, molar or volume; unknown if unstated.
Unit or notation for additive loading.
Basis or denominator for additive loading.

Qualifier attached to the reported thickness or thickness range.

Atmosphere during active-layer annealing.
Annealing-treatment method, such as thermal or solvent-vapour annealing.
Reported atmosphere during device or active-layer preparation.
Reported preparation-solution concentration; the solute and total/component basis follow source context.
